- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.50), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% to account for reversal.  
- Model consistently overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days) — cap forecast peak at 2–3% above recent high.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion within 5–7 days after a spike, model should be adjusted downward by 1–2% per day until trend stabilizes.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model often fails to capture early mean reversion — apply a 1–2% downward bias if sentiment turns neutral or negative within 7 days.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag — add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to compensate for delayed reaction.
